result.title: ReTrace: Visual Backtracking for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
result.comment: Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026, forthcoming
result.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) encode images into dense visual token sequences, creating substantial attention and KV-cache overhead. Existing visual token compression methods reduce this cost by pruning low-saliency tokens in shallow layers, but this practice couples temporary computational deactivation with irreversible information deletion. We show that this coupling breaks an intrinsic inference pattern in MLLMs. Through layer-wise attention analysis, we identify \textbf{Visual Backtracking}: visual pivots remain spatially stable, yet in middle layers they actively retrieve context from tokens that appeared unimportant earlier. Thus, early low-saliency tokens can be inactive for computation while still being useful for later reasoning. Motivated by this finding, we propose \textbf{ReTrace}, a backtracking-aware compression framework that introduces a dormant token state. ReTrace caches non-pivot tokens outside expensive layer-wise computation, restores them during the backtracking window, and prunes only after their information has been absorbed. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 demonstrate nearly 90\% reductions in FLOPs and KV cache, a 2.83$\times$ prefilling speedup, and strong performance retention across complex vision-language benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过逐层注意力分析发现 MLLM 中的「Visual Backtracking」现象：中层会重新取用早期看似不重要的视觉 token，据此提出 ReTrace，用可休眠 token 状态把非枢轴 token 移出昂贵计算、在回溯窗口内恢复、待信息被吸收后再剪枝，在 Qwen2.5-VL 与 InternVL3 上大幅降低 FLOPs 与 KV cache。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接涉及视觉细节是否保留在内部状态、以及剪枝「暂停计算」与「删除信息」耦合导致的信息坍缩问题，其分层注意力诊断与视觉证据筛选、动态计算成本的研究兴趣相关，可供核查其对 latent 状态保留与长度泛化的启示。
